requirements.evidence: The invite table/model/factory/mail, sendInvite (rate limit, duplicate/member checks, race handling), PendingInvites accept/decline, and the members-page invite form are implemented and tested (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:65-137, app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:18-70, app/Models/EntityInvite.php, database/migrations/2026_10_29_035323_create_entity_invites_table.php). However, the member-details and removal modals are rendered after the card root (resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:82-84 and :109), so requirements 3-5 (openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval UI) are structurally outside the component root.

conventions.evidence: Uses EntityInvitePolicy and EntityPolicy::manageMembers for authorization (app/Policies/EntityInvitePolicy.php:15-39, app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:59-66), #[Validate] on inviteEmail/inviteRole, a generated reversible migration, docs/CHANGELOG updates, and {{ }} escaping. Deviations: new domain writes stay in Livewire components instead of app/Actions/*, memberRole uses inline $this->validate([...]) instead of #[Validate] (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:202), and the modals lack dialog semantics/a11y attributes.

security.evidence: Every action resolves the model and authorizes it (Members.php:65-137, :142-158, :164-173, :186-225, :230-235, :248-270; PendingInvites.php:18-70), inviteEmail/inviteRole/memberRole are validated, EntityInvitePolicy restricts accept/decline to the invitee and cancel to managers, the unique (entity_id,email) and #[Fillable] are deliberate, and Blade output uses {{ }} throughout.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: SendInviteTest (validation, duplicate member/pending, expiry replacement, race, rate limit, cancel, employee 403), PendingInvitesTest (case-insensitive list, accept idempotency/no duplicate, expiry, unauthorized accept/decline, onboarding hr/switcher), MemberDetailsTest (foreign id, owner read-only, last manager, tamper), EntityInvite/Mail tests. Gap: modal tests inspect only server ->html() (tests/Feature/Entity/MemberDetailsTest.php:42), so the multi-root rendering failure is not caught, and no test calls saveRole as a demoted manager.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses x-input, EntityInvite::normalizeEmail, closeMember() and managerCount() (Members.php:186-225, :272-294); no new service/repository layers. Minor duplication: the two modal scaffolds are copied in members.blade.php, and isInviteConflict() matches driver error text (Members.php:316-326).

readability.evidence: Clear, focused methods with docblocks (Members.php sendInvite/cancelInvite/openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval; PendingInvites accept/decline), consistent naming and sibling Blade/Livewire style; no debug code or dead code.

scope.evidence: All changed files serve the invite/members feature (models, policy, mail, migration, factory, Livewire, Blade, lang, docs, CHANGELOG, tests); no unrelated refactors or speculative features.

issues.explanation: The card root closes at line 82 and the two conditional modals start at line 84 and around line 109, so the component view has multiple root elements; Livewire requires a single root and only morphs that root, so the member-details and removal-confirmation modals will not render/update after openMember/confirmRemoval, breaking requirements 3-5.
The new domain writes (creating an invite, accepting it into a membership) are implemented inline in Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* as the project's domain-write convention requires.
memberRole is validated with an inline $this->validate([...]) rule instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern, so its rules live away from the other validated public properties.
The new 'Expires :expiration' UI string is not added to lang/pt_BR.json, so the Portuguese UI falls back to English for the expiry line (the members invite table has the same issue).
The modal tests only inspect the server-rendered ->html(); they do not exercise the component root/DOM behavior, so the multi-root rendering failure goes undetected.
The Bulma modals lack role="dialog"/aria-modal/labelledby and focus handling, so the new dialogs are not accessible to assistive technology.
The template switches to __('ui.email'), but this diff does not add that key; verify it exists in both ui.php files, otherwise the aria-label and table header show the raw key.

review.summary: The change adds the entity-invite domain, queued markdown mail, pending-invite component, manager-only members page and docs/tests, with good authorization and validation coverage. The main blocker is that the members Blade view puts the details and removal modals outside the card root, giving the Livewire component multiple roots, so the new modal UI will not render/update after openMember/confirmRemoval. Minor convention gaps (no Actions for the new writes, inline memberRole validation, missing pt_BR 'Expires' string) also need fixing.
